personality.description: This person prefers familiar routines and proven methods, and may be skeptical of new ideas unless they are clearly useful. They are not especially orderly, so their habits can be inconsistent and they may forget details or let tasks slip, yet they usually stay calm rather than getting flustered. When facing moral dilemmas, they tend to choose the most practical and conventional option, but they will voice their own view if they think it matters. In group discussions, they are quiet and reserved, speaking briefly and directly in small, comfortable settings rather than in lively, expansive exchanges.
traits: has assertively moved up the ranks into positions of leadership
prioritizes having control and authority over others
makes quick and definitive decisions, and once a decision is made it is usually final
has their own views of how tasks should be accomplished
uses reward and punishment to get people to follow their ideas
